rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for an object question, including after a Cantonese preposition such as 同, 對, or 向.

example.english: Whom do you want to have dinner with?
example.jyutping: nei5 soeng2 tung4 bin1 go3 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use this relative-clause pattern when referring to a person previously mentioned, with the object understood inside the clause.

example.english: The person whom I asked to come and help carry the bag just now is my older brother.
example.traditional: 頭先我叫嚟幫手拎袋嘅人係我阿哥。
example.jyutping: tau4 sin1 ngo5 giu3 lai4 bong1 sau2 ling1 doi6 ge3 jan4 hai6 ngo5 aa3 go1

rows.note: Use this for an indefinite person or people in contexts where English means “whomever” or “any person.”

example.english: You can bring anyone whom you want along.
example.jyutping: nei5 soeng2 daai3 jam6 ho4 jan4 lei4 dou1 dak1
